scheme_name: Financial Assistance to Revive, Preserve and Protect Goan Maand Culture
description:
The Financial Assistance to Revive, Preserve and Protect Goan Maand Culture scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in the year 2021. 

This initiative aims to safeguard and promote the traditional Maand culture of Goa, which is an integral part of the state's rich heritage. 

The Maand culture encompasses a unique form of music and dance that is performed during various festivals and cultural events in Goa. 

The scheme was introduced in response to the growing concern over the decline of traditional art forms due to modernization and changing social dynamics. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial support to artists and cultural organizations involved in the preservation and promotion of Maand culture. 

The government aims to allocate a total budget of ₹5 crore for this initiative over a span of five years. 

This budget is intended to support various activities including training programs, workshops, and performances that showcase Maand culture. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness among the younger generation about the importance of preserving their cultural heritage. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to conduct at least 50 workshops annually that focus on teaching the Maand music and dance forms. 

Additionally, the government aims to support at least 100 artists and cultural groups each year through financial grants and assistance. 

The benefits under this scheme include direct financial assistance to artists, which can range from ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 depending on the nature of the project or activity. 

Cultural organizations can receive grants up to ₹2 lakh for organizing events that promote Maand culture. 

Eligibility criteria for individuals applying for financial assistance include being a resident of Goa and having a demonstrated involvement in Maand culture. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age and should have a background in performing arts or cultural activities related to Maand. 

For cultural organizations, registration under the Societies Registration Act or similar legal framework is mandatory. 

The application process for individuals involves submitting a detailed proposal outlining the project, along with proof of residency and any relevant documentation showcasing their work in Maand culture. 

Cultural organizations must provide their registration certificate along with a project proposal and a budget estimate for the planned activities. 

Applications can be submitted online through the official website of the Goa Department of Art and Culture. 

The deadline for submitting applications is typically set for the end of each financial year, with specific announcements made through official notifications. 

Disbursement of funds is usually completed within three months of the approval of the application. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

For inquiries or assistance, individuals can contact the department at their official office located in Panaji, Goa. 

The contact number for the Department of Art and Culture is +91-832-222-1234. 

The scheme also emphasizes collaboration with educational institutions to integrate Maand culture into their curriculum. 

Schools and colleges are encouraged to participate in workshops and cultural exchanges that focus on Goan traditions. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides resources for documentation and archiving of Maand performances. 

This includes audio-visual recordings that can be used for educational and promotional purposes. 

The government has also partnered with local NGOs to facilitate outreach programs aimed at engaging the community in cultural activities. 

Statistics indicate that since the launch of the scheme, there has been a noticeable increase in participation in Maand-related events by approximately 30%. 

Furthermore, the scheme has contributed to the revival of interest in traditional music among the youth, with over 200 new participants joining workshops in the past year. 

The government plans to expand the scope of the scheme by introducing an annual Maand festival that showcases performances from various artists and groups. 

This festival aims to attract tourists and promote Goa as a cultural destination, thereby providing additional economic benefits to local artists. 

The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India to promote and preserve intangible cultural heritage as outlined in the UNESCO Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage. 

The scheme also contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by promoting inclusive and sustainable economic growth through cultural tourism. 

Overall, the Financial Assistance to Revive, Preserve and Protect Goan Maand Culture scheme represents a significant effort by the Government of Goa to ensure that the rich cultural heritage of the state is preserved for future generations. 

Through targeted financial assistance and community engagement, the scheme aims to create a vibrant cultural landscape that honors and celebrates the unique traditions of Goa. 

The success of this initiative will depend on the active participation of local communities, artists, and cultural organizations in promoting and preserving the Maand culture. 

By fostering a sense of pride and ownership in their cultural heritage, the government hopes to inspire a new generation to embrace and carry forward the traditions of Goa. 

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance to Revive, Preserve and Protect Goan Maand Culture scheme is a comprehensive initiative designed to support the preservation of an essential aspect of Goan identity. 

With specific financial allocations and measurable objectives, the scheme aims to create a sustainable framework for the revival and promotion of Maand culture in Goa. 

As the program progresses, it will be crucial to monitor its impact on the cultural landscape of the state and make necessary adjustments to ensure its long-term success.
